newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Crean warns H1 earnings will be down on '96.
newsitem.headline: Crean warns H1 earnings will be down on '96.

text.p: Irish industrial holding company James Crean Plc on Friday warned that first half earnings would be down relative to last year.

Crean said this reflected a number of factors including weakness in the UK industrial electrical market while first-half results from the poultry business will be affected by supply problems and a ban on fowl meat exports to EU countries.
But the company said in a statement that its frozen meals business was performing strongly while results from its paper, print and packaging division would be in line with last year.
Crean also said the trading outlook for the second half of the year was more encouraging.
"Although the UK industrial electrical market is likely to continue weak, a better performance is expected from the remainder of the group's businesses," it said.
But it added that a number of planned disposals would lead to a loss of profit contribution which will not be recovered until funds have been re-invested in the group's core businesses.
"This will adversely affect EPS (earnings per share) performance in the second half," Crean said.
